chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Mas'ada, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Recitation of the Quran from the Mushaf lightens the punishment from the parents, even if they were both disbelievers.'

key_terms.الْمُصْحَفِ: The Mushaf: the physical written copy of the Quran, as distinct from recitation from memory. Classical scholars noted special merit in looking at the physical pages of the Quran.
key_terms.الْوَالِدَيْنِ: The two parents: dual form emphasizing both mother and father equally.
key_terms.تُخَفِّفُ الْعَذَابَ: Lightens/reduces the punishment: a concept in Islamic eschatology where the deeds of the living can benefit the deceased in the grave or in the afterlife.
key_terms.كَافِرَيْنِ: Two disbelievers: dual form; the use of the conditional 'even if they were disbelievers' is theologically significant, suggesting benefit even across the barrier of unbelief.

ai.seo_question: Can reciting the Quran from the Mushaf benefit non-Muslim parents in the afterlife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that a child's recitation of the Quran from the physical Mushaf benefits even non-Muslim deceased parents by reducing their torment in the afterlife. This hadith emphasizes the immense spiritual power of Quran recitation and the duty of filial piety that transcends religious boundaries. The specific mention of reading from the Mushaf — the physical book — underscores the particular merit assigned to engaging with the sacred text in its written form.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Mas’ada, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from his grandfather, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Recitation of the Quran in the Parchment would lighten the Punishment from the parents, and even if they were both disbelievers’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Mas’adah from al-Hassan ibn Rashid from his grandfather from abu ‘Abd Allah  (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Reading of the Holy Quran from a copy relieves suffering punishment of one’s parents even if they are unbelievers.”
